status: User accepted the 1 exact diagnostic sites on 2026-10-07. Focused qualification and its recorded limits are unchanged. Full RPM and native architecture qualification remain separate gates.
root_cause: GCC does not connect the nonempty cases vector with the assignment of current_if_false before every insertion. The final pointer is read only when more than two cases have been collected.
source_review: Both supported branch forms assign current_if_true/current_if_false before appending to cases and false_blocks.
An early break before any assignment leaves cases empty and reaches no_change. A later early break retains the last initialized false block, which becomes the default continuation.
EmitSwitch is reachable only after cases.size()>2 and duplicate-case rejection, so at least three pointer assignments occurred.

coverage.matrix: Cascades of length 1–7; equality and inverted zero-test first branches; all three hint modes; optimization bypass; early exits for wrong comparison, wrong constant, impure continuation and differing variable; duplicate-case rejection; truncated terminal blocks. Verify switch destinations, sorted cases, inlined blocks and exact default continuation.
coverage.memory: Both runs have zero errors; all 12560102 allocations freed per run.
coverage.actual_node: Turbofan-verified functions cover lengths 1–7, duplicate values, side effects that must not be hoisted, and mixed input variables. Independent sequential reference checks results and side-effect counts over signed 32-bit boundary values.

limits: The entire ReduceInputGraphBranch body is verbatim, including bailouts and case sorting. Graph operations, block purity and switch emission use typed adapters.
Native checks validate destinations and initialization. They do not model instruction selection, graph cloning, or branch-hint performance heuristics.
Actual JavaScript checks confirm the Turbofan execution tier and semantics; they do not assert that every generated graph is transformed into a switch.
No runtime patch, suppression or compiler-flag change is proposed.
